recipes.name: Oma’s Rhubarb Cake
ingredients_raw: 0.25 teaspoon ground cinnamon, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking dish.
To make the cake: Stir together flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in eggs and sour cream until smooth, then fold in rhubarb.
Pour into the prepared dish and spread evenly.
To make the streusel: Stir together sugar and butter in a medium bowl until smooth. Stir in flour until mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle mixture on top of cake, then dust lightly with cinnamon.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Oma’s Rhubarb Cake
raw_recipe.description: This rhubarb cake is packed with flavorful, fresh springtime rhubarb and topped with a buttery cinnamon streusel for a moist and delicious dessert.

video.description: Deliciously sweet, tart, and crumbly rhubarb cake!

review.reviewBody: What a winner! Noticing the recipe called for no fat, I was tempted to add a 1/2 stick of butter and I'm so glad I didn't and stuck to the recipe as written, only adding 1 tsp. of vanilla to the batter. This was SO nice and moist with a perfect amount of rhubarb. Any more, I fear, might have made this soggy rather than cakey, particularly after the first day. I was afraid of glopping on the cinnamon by shaking it over the topping, so rather than take a chance I mixed maybe 3/4 tsp. of cinnamon in with the topping ingredients. Good call I think! This is simply a great, old fashioned coffee cake - nice balance of rich, moist cake, delicately flavored with rhubarb and topped with a buttery, crackly, streusel. Grandmas always seem to know how to do it best!

Easy, simple and delicious! I didn't have sour cream on hand so I substituted plain yogurt. I used 3/4 cup of packed brown sugar instead of white sugar (personal taste preference) and also added 1/4 cup of chopped walnuts to the topping. I'll make this again. UPDATE May 8, 2011: If anyone is interested in cutting back calories - I've made this using 3/4 cup sugar in the cake and only half the topping. Still delicious with a crusty crunchy top. This may depend on how sour your rhubarb is. Also, try using a cup of red currants in place of 1 cup of rhubarb.

I didn't have sour cream, so I used plain milk with 1 T vinegar....it turned out GREAT! You need to leave the milk and vinegar out for about 1/2 hour, so it curdles the milk a bit. Other than that, I made just like the recipe. It is SOOO DELICIOUS! THANK YOU!!!

I grabbed this recipe as a last-minute dessert option and used frozen cranberries and apples instead of rhubarb (2 cups cranberries; 2 apples diced). It got RAVE reviews from everyone so I will make it again, for sure. I didn't have a 9x13 pan so split the recipe in two 8" rounds. Baked it about 10 minutes longer than suggested. I served one on a cake plate (with ice cream on the side) which made for a pretty presentation. I used others' suggestions re brown sugar instead of white for the streusal topping.

Since I can't do eggs or dairy, I made this vegan by using Just Egg for the eggs, Tofutti sour cream, and Earth's Balance buttery stick for the butter. It came out delicious!! Hubby is from Poland and says it tasted very close to the version his mom made. I only used 2 cups of diced rhubarb and it was plenty, but next time will use the 3 cups recommended in the recipe. A1so followed other user's suggestions and put 1 tsp. cinnamon in the topping mixture instead of sprinkled on top and added 1 tsp. vanilla. Will definitely make it again. Very moist and tasty. Added bonus - some vegan coconut whipped cream on top! Perfect summer dessert.

I used five cups of rhubarb and added 1/4 c flour due to it having extra moisture from the rhubarb. I also scaled back the sugar inside the recipe and in the topping (as I like my rhubarb a little more tart.) I also added extra cinnamon like two teaspoons full if not more as I love cinnamon. The changes are just my preference and I'm sure the cake is fine without any changes but always like to share my ideas. This was so moist and flavorful and a very dense cake. We loved it! I also sprinkled the rhubarb with a little flour this helps with it not sinking to the bottom of the cake batter after adding.

Amazing taste and easy to make with staple ingredients! First time using rhubarb from the garden. I’ve made it 3 times. Each time substituting sour cream with a variety of different wet ingredients. First time with only cottage cheese, 2nd time with 1/2 Greek yogurt & 1/2 sour cream, 3rd time with 1/2 milk & 1 tsp white vinegar for buttermilk substitute and 1/2 sour cream (wet ingredients always = 1 cup). Always added cinnamon to both cake and topping. Used 1/2 brown sugar and 1/2 white and used less because I didn’t want it to be too sweet. Baked for 1 hour (maybe my oven is off as it’s old) until tooth pick comes out clean. In any case, always turned out fabulous & family/friends agreed. Will make next time using different fruit as rhubarb is done for the season. Thanks for sharing!

I have an Air BnB and actually offer fresh-baked breakfast treats every day. This recipe -- delicious, simple, quick -- will go into my regular rotation. So yummy. So nice not to have to beat or melt butter for the cake part. I whirled the butter and flour in a small food processor, then pulsed in the sugar (I used half dark brown) and the cinnamon. Came out great. I'm pretty sure it will be good with other fruits as well.

I had read about the substitution of brown sugar for white. I chose to go with 1/3 white cane sugar and 2/3 dark brown sugar. I also added a nice shake of allspice and about a 1/4 tsp each of baking soda and baking powder for the streusel. The 3 cups of rhubarb is what makes this recipe one to bake again (and again) 😁😋

Tastes great, esp w all brown sugar for topping, plus a little allspice. Did vanilla extract in the batter too. Had no sour cream and only 3/4 c of yogurt, so I added 1/4 c blueberry yogurt to batter as well. Not bad! DO NOT freak out about the dry-to-liquid ingredients ratio when making the batter. Fresh rhubarb has tons of liquid in it and all will be well.

I modified this recipe slightly to make a healthier version, using whole meal flour and 1 cup of coconut sugar instead of the 1.25 cups regular sugar, also half the streusel topping and again with coconut sugar. I actually think it is better with the coconut palm sugar as it gives it more if a caramelized flavour. I also often use yogurt in place of sour cream. It’s been a big hit with everyone who has tried it.

I have an Oma too (who was renowned for her cooking and baking) so figured this recipe had to be good. It's amazing...the perfect crunch on top, soft and moist on the inside. The only change I made was adding cinnamon to the batter as well as using half white sugar and half brown sugar. Will be making this regularly.

After following as written which was great! I tried again by added more rhubarb and reduced sugar by 1/4 c in batter and halved the amount in the streusel topping as I prefer things less sweet. Also replaced 1)3 of flour with bean flour to add a bit of protein. Excellent use of rhubarb especially for folks leary or unfamiliar with an old time fruit.
Delish! I used plain Greek yogurt in place of sour cream. No other changes and it was loved by all. Thanks for the recipe👏🏻

Made this delicious cake with Rhubarb my neighbour gave me . 12 hours later 2 of us have devoured 1/2 of the 9x13 pan quantity! Easiest recipe to follow, and no power gadget required except the oven! Definitely a keeper recipe!

I made this and also used plain Greek yogurt. I forgot the flour in the streusel topping. But I wasn't mad about the slightly crunchy caramelly topping. My family loved it too. My husband likes very few fruits and vegetables, so when he asked what the favor in it was, I told him rhubarb! I think he was surprised too. The next time I make it, I will also add vanilla like the others mentioned in comments and I will definitely make sure I do the streusel topping correctly. Though I feel like this cake is so special that it is lovely with all kinds of variations. :) One thought I had was to maybe spoon some strawberry jam on it before eating it. Can't wait to try it with my morning coffee.

Best rhubarb cake I’ve made. I didn’t have enough rhubarb so I added an apple to bring up quantity to 3 cups. I did add a splash of vanilla but did it make a difference, who knows? Everything else was as per the recipe and it was very moist and tasted great.

My family absolutely loved this. It is dense and moist from the sour cream. Simple to make. Crunchy and sweet on top, but not too much. I made almond-flavored whipped cream to go with and it was a quiet room....
Great Flavor and easy to make!
Very good and all the ingredients already in the house.
